questions.question: What is the Coriolis force?
questions.solution_html:
• The Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by the rotation of the Earth, which deflects
  • the path of moving objects such as winds and ocean currents. Definition- (1 mark) . Northern
  • Hemisphere- winds are deflected to the right. Southern hemisphere- winds are deflected to
  • left- (1 mark) .

questions.question: Explain different types of anticyclones.
questions.solution_html:
• Types- 1. Cold anticyclones - after originating in the arctic regions cold anticyclones
  • advance in easterly and south-easterly directions. Low thickness, smaller, very few higher
  • than 3000m. 2. Warm anticyclones- originate in the belt of subtropical high pressure where
  • winds diverge in opposite directions. dynamically induced, large in size, sluggish
  • movement, associated with light wind, cloudless sky and clear weather. 3. Blocking
  • anticyclone- develop due to obstruction in the air circulation in the upper troposphere.
  • Small in size, moves very slowly. Detailed Explanation- (8 marks) .
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain precession of the Earth’s axis and its impact on seasons and climate.
questions.solution_html:
• Precession is the wobbling motion of earth’s rotational axis, similar to a spinning top.
  • Caused by gravitational forces of the Sun and Moon on Earth’s equatorial bulge. Completes
  • one cycle in about 26,000 years. Changes the position of stars over long periods. Influences
  • long-term climate changes (Milankovitch cycles) . Definition- (1 mark) . Explanation- 3.5
  • marks. Significance- (2.5 marks) . Diagram- (1 mark) .

questions.question: Discuss the three main types of rainfall—convectional, orographic, and cyclonic in detail.
questions.solution_html:
• Types of precipitation - Convectional rainfall , Orographic rainfall, Cyclonic or frontal
  • rainfall.
  • Convectional rainfall - occurring due to thermal convection currents caused due to
  • insolational heating of ground surface – (4marks) .
  • Orographic rainfall- occuring due to ascent of air forced by mountain barrier- (4 marks) .
  • Cyclonic or frontal rainfall - occurring due to upward movement of air caused by
  • convergence of extensive air masses- (4 marks) .
